To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
phasic dopamine release in the nucleus accummens symmetrically encodes reward prediction error signals.

phasic dopamine release in the nucleus accummens core of rats is symmetrically modulated by reward prediction error (positive and negative), is temporally correlated with reward, is correlated with behavioral choices, and is correlated with behavioral performance.

phasic dopamine release encodes a reward-prediction error signal in the rat nucleus accumbens, that this encoding is bidirectional, that the encoding of positive and of negative reward-prediction errors is symmetrical, and that the encoding of reward-prediction-error signals in dopamine release in the nucleus accombens is sufficient to support the reinforcement learning process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain makes predictions about the future, and how these predictions are updated through experience.
understanding the role of dopamine in learning about reward.
the neural mechanisms of reinforcement learning.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
phasic dopamine release in the nucleus accummens symmetrically encodes a reward-prediction error term.

phasic dopamine release in the nucleus accummens symmetrically encodes a reward-prediction error (RPE).
The main takeaway from our work is that

the dopamine signal is not a unidirectional positive RPE signal as is often assumed, but instead it is a bidirectional prediction error signal that encodes both the positive and negative aspects of the RPE.
dopamine release in the nucleus accummens symmetrically encodes the full range of prediction errors that are required for reinforcement learning.
the dopamine system is capable of encoding the full range of prediction errors that are necessary for reinforcement learning, even though it has low baseline activity.
